A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VVS work. Their complete main texts and supplementary materials, including equations, algorithms, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation benchmarks, token-selection and feature-staleness experiments, and Lumina-mGPT qualitative results in Sections 3–5 and the supplement.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Lumina-mGPT similarity diagnostics and quantitative system-overhead reporting.

M1.justification: Appendix Algorithm 2 changes the stated initialization from target-produced tokens/features to a drafter-produced candidate, reorganizes feature retrieval, and removes explicit concatenation of previously unverified tokens before the target-model call. These are localized procedural changes in the pseudocode. The core design remains unchanged, and the omission is not reconciled with the post-verification procedure retained in Section 4.1 and Figure 5.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate text-to-image generation using MS-COCO and the same qualitative prompts. Lumina-mGPT already appears in v1's supplementary Figure 9; v2's additional diagnostics do not introduce a new dataset, task, or input scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 7 retain the same comparators, including vanilla AR, EAGLE-2, and LANTERN. The relaxed-SD comparison in supplementary Figure 9 is also retained. Newly cited background works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 5 adds an overhead assessment comparing similarity-computation time with AR decoding for Lumina-mGPT-7B on one RTX 4090. The existing 5,000-sample COCO evaluation, temperature, relaxation settings, quality metrics, and A40-based Table 1 timing protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 extends token-path and feature-staleness similarity analysis to Lumina-mGPT, supplementing its existing qualitative evaluation. New supplementary Section 5 analyzes computation and memory overhead. Existing verification-redundancy, token-selection, truncation, and feature-reuse ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. V2's discussion of relaxation-induced uncertainty concerns generation noise, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical values in Tables 1–6 are unchanged, as are Figure 9's examples and speedups. Figure 10 newly reports Lumina-mGPT feature similarities, including 0.444 at staleness 9 and 0.607 at staleness 1. Supplementary Section 5 adds the 6-second similarity-computation versus 70-second AR-decoding comparison and under-1% uniform-scheduling overhead.

T1.justification: The probability formulation, truncation rule, weighted similarity definition, and TPF equation retain their mathematical content. Explaining the existing path-set symbol and adding practical cache-size accounting introduce no new formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: partial verification skipping, verification redundancy, stale-feature reuse, and approximately 2.8-fold fewer target-model forward passes with competitive generation quality. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New supplementary Section 6 explains metric improvements through stochastic sampling and visual-token interchangeability, while explicitly acknowledging lossy approximation and possible recall degradation from skipping verification. Section 5 additionally argues that fixed draft-tree depth makes relative overhead decrease with target-model scale.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link in the abstract and discloses overhead-profiling hardware and model size. Supplementary Section 5 specifies caching five 1280-dimensional LlamaGen features in BF16, with a stated footprint below 100 kB. Algorithm 2's implementation description is also revised.

R1.justification: V2 adds four background references: a decentralized-LLM-training survey, Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models, DICE, and a diffusion-model survey. The introduction adds diffusion-model context, while positioning relative to existing speculative-decoding methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and clarity edits in the abstract, introduction, and method descriptions, updates the affiliation, and adds acknowledgments. Two supplementary sections expand the narrative, while the main section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel Figure 10, relocates Figure 7 and adds Pareto shading and a dashed frontier, and changes supplementary speed-column labels to tau and MAL. Algorithm 2 is reformatted and shortened. Figure 10's caption incorrectly also mentions a panel (c).

improvement.justification: The added Lumina-mGPT diagnostics, overhead accounting, code-access information, and explicit discussion of recall losses modestly strengthen evidence and transparency. Existing benchmark results are unchanged. Algorithm 2 becomes less explicit about post-verification, weakening documentation consistency; however, Section 4.1 and Figure 5 retain that explanation, limiting this drawback relative to the additions.
